facts: What kin I do for ye, $N?
The Valley of Trials will temper even the weakest into a warrior worthy to join the Horde. Those who cannot rise to its tests will be left to bake in the scorching desert sun.
Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.
Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?
You haven't lived until you've looked down on the world from the back of a wind rider.
Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?
My wind riders are trained to fly quickly through the hot Barrens air.
I do what me can to train you in the priestly ways, if that what you be here for.
If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.
If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.

Please do not touch the vials unless you intend to purchase one.

Fingerprints ruin the value, you see.
You won't find better equipment anywhere else!

<Jim'bek locks eyes with you as he takes a deep puff from his hookah.>

'Ello, mon. Need a rug? A blanket? Or just some cloth for your next project? I got you.

The Wind Spirits have left us. 

Now, only mindless echoes remain. Be wary, however. These winds are neither kind, nor gentle.

<As you approach the enormous cyclone construct, you hear a faint buzzing emanating from beneath its massive armor plates. If you listen carefully, you think you might be able to hear a few words being formed but they are too distorted to make out.>

Slay your enemies and swoon your paramours with this one weird trick.

If you follow the path of the $c{rogue}, I can teach you... for a cost, of course.
What may I do for you, fellow windshaper?
<Constable Aonda wears an intense look on her face, clearly deep in thought.>

Alas, I have prattled on long enough. Seek out my apprentice Ayessa Dawnsinger in the port of Valanaar if you find yourself out that way. She still hears the song--if only faintly. I am old and much of my power has left me. Ayessa represents the future of our people and the path we must now walk to survive. It's up to her and young skyborne such as yourself to carry the hopes for our people forward.

Greetings, child. I am Illaya Amberwind and I am the Elder Windshaper here on Zephras Isle. It's always nice to meet young new faces that make their way down from the grove.

Don't let this old shaman hold you up, no doubt you've got many adventures to see to. Do feel free to stop by later if you'd like.

In all of our years dealing with the wind spirits, at no point did they speak of the Windlord as a figure of reverence. They acknowledged the existence of a being named Al'Akir, but they avoided invoking his name, almost as if they feared him. 

Even if this Al'Akir is an all-powerful "Windlord" or ruler of the wind elementals, my centuries of communion with the spirits has convinced me that at the very least he is not universally loved amongst the denizens of Skywall. I fear that attempting to treat with Al'Akir could merely hasten our doom.

Many disagree on this point. I believe that simple communication is the key. The songs of the wind rang so clearly to us when the spirits were still here. Since they left, it's grown quiet and our power as windshapers has weakened. 

However, there are those of us who can still hear something. A hushed tone. Fragments of a melody. Those that can still hear and see into the elemental planes must grow in strength. I believe that is the key to our salvation.

The Cult? They are zealots and killers. They believe that we are being punished for some unspecific sin. The reality is that those that lead them are opportunists leftover from a dubious order of so-called "Priests" of Al'Akir, the Windlord. 

They now find themselves in a position to weaponize the fear of our people to consolidate their own power... and they have been quick to do so.

Where to begin? Our home is failing. The wards have fallen and the three provinces have begun to drift apart. There was a time not long ago when the spires of Shen'dramar were visible from the western watchtower. No longer. The anchor pylons are weakening, and if the chains finally break...

Why is this happening? Put simply, the spirits of the wind just... vanished. They were there one day, and they were gone the next. I can't quite describe the feeling that we windshapers felt when it happened. It was as if a great silence fell over all of us and then... a profound absence.

The petty wraiths you've likely encountered out there are just shades of the glory of the true spirits of wind. Non-sentient, aimless, and a far cry from the kindly spirits we lived in harmony alongside for thousands of years.

You must remember that while this realm has been our home for millennia, we will always be somewhat alien to this place. We are not in the terrestrial world that birthed our people. We are in the realm of Skywall, a part of the elemental plane.

We arrived here as the guests of spirits with whom we found common cause in ages past. Now that we Shen'dorei find ourselves bereft of their presence--and potentially--their protection, there's no telling how the other denizens of this plane may perceive us.
Greetings, $c{rogue}. Do you come seeking the blessings of the Windlord?
If you need training as a cook, I have a few tips and tricks I could pass on! Ho ho! Throw on an apron and let's get started!

I'm in charge of Shen'dar Village operations, and there's a lot of things to keep track of around here. Between bandits, cultists, and other random incidents that pop up, keeping this village afloat is a lot of work.
I can teach you to swing a blacksmith's hammer, if you are willing to learn.
You're not bad, but let me show you a few tricks you might find handy.
Greetings, I am Ayessa Dawnsinger, the current Grand Skyseer of the Windshapers. What may I do for you?

The clothcraft of the Shen'dorei is a harmonious imitation of the flowing, carefree currents of the winds. While the spirits have left us, and I know not when I may see them dance once more... I find great comfort in my art, if only as a distraction.

I can teach you to work the cloth as well, if you'd like to learn?
Welcome to Shen'dar Village, some of the best fishing this side of the mountain range. If you are looking to catch fish, I can teach you, for a price.
I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.
<The corpse lying before you is covered in scorches and burn marks. He seems to be clutching something in his hand.>

Our kind are rare these days, but there are those who still dream in emerald amongst the shen'dorei.

Keep your eyes open in the forest. The right light can reveal that which is hidden, protected by the north wind.

Slay your enemies and swoon your paramours with this one weird trick.

If you follow the path of the $c{rogue}, I can teach you... for a cost, of course.
<The man lying before you shifts uncomfortably. He's recovering from some very nasty wounds.>
It's always great to see you, $N.
May I help you locate something, citizen?
That trainer can be found on the southeastern edge of town, near the High Order's dock.
I bur ealdor aelgestron thor A an, goibon hir nuff. Mandos Uden ador se ru nud ador ealdor A dana ador. Nud ealdor me garde nuff Skilde Regenthor. Ru ealdor bur borne nud uden, ruff gol.
Thank you for your help. Make sure you let my husband know that the farm is safe.
The Windfield Orchard has seen better days...

The spirits of the wind may have left us, but the power of the elements is not entirely out of reach for those with the patience to seek them out.

If you are initiated in the ways of the shaman, I can help you grasp them.

Slay your enemies and swoon your paramours with this one weird trick.

If you follow the path of the $c{rogue}, I can teach you... for a cost, of course.
Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?

Have you heard of what's become of Ban'aethal? The peacekeepers are warning people to stay away from the ruins and the Shadowgale Forest entirely.

I overheard someone at the inn talking about seeing malevolent wind spirits that seemed to be little more than a hazy outline, as if they were... hollowed out somehow.

Gives me the chills just thinking about such a thing.
<The two cultists nearby are talking. You might be able to learn something if you hide behind this wardrobe and eavesdrop.>
I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.
Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?
<Riaani seems to be intently focused on his work on the wind construct.>
We've had trouble with shipments going missing across Azeroth. If you find any, I'd appreciate if you could return them to me.

Greetings and well met, $N! Your arrival is timely, and we here at the Durotar Supply and Logistics company are always in need of new contractors.

If you are someone with a knack for gathering useful materials or the skills to craft something from scratch, you have a place here.

Please let me know if you have any questions.
I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.
It appears the winds have brought you my way! I am happy to train you in the ways of cooking if you have the inclination to learn.
Ko, i waldir Regenthor. A garde lo thor ve borne nud hamerung ador garde bur agol cynegold.
Va, i waldir Eloderung. Ash nud vassild va noth ko i valesh hamerung? Algos A bur uden nud i wirsh ko bor?
Ko, i waldir Regenthor. A garde lo thor ve borne nud hamerung ador garde bur agol cynegold.
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?

You might think that just because we live on a floating island, there would be no need for miners like me. After so many thousands of years, however, we still manage to dig up a lot of interesting things.

It's almost like there's some invisible force, constantly creating new mineral deposits every so often. That's magic for you though, right?

Regardless, if you need training as a miner, then I'm your shen'dorei.
Welcome to the Bank of Valanaar. We can secure your belongings and valuables here should you so desire. Do you wish to access your deposit box?
Do you seek the blessings of the Windlord?

All of the skyborne islands became destabilized and began to move apart a few years ago. If that wasn't bad enough, now large pieces of Zephras are beginning to fall away. It's hard to imagine your home falling into the sky, but that is my reality now.

Another fresh face! Welcome to Azeroth, pal. Come back and see me if you need help setting yourself up for success.

Bring money.

The first order of business will be to put a little strength in your backbone. I could send you out to the Barrens to hunt kodo, but well, in all honesty, you're more useful to us alive than dead.

I believe you would find a good match with the mottled boars you'll find to the north of here.
Kill 10 Mottled Boars then return to Gornek at the Den.

Hmmm, not bad, $N. But don't let it get to your head...you'll fight tougher than boars in your career.

Nonetheless, you've proven yourself well, and your next trial will be against a considerably more dangerous opponent, so you'll need some extra protection.

Powerful warrior and awkward novice alike have fallen to the venomous sting of the scorpid. You will find large numbers of scorpids northwest of here. Bring me ten of their tails as proof of your prowess in battle.

The antidote for their sting is actually made from venom extracted from their stingers. We keep large quantities of antidote for scorpid venom on hand to heal young bloods just like you...

But I'm sure you won't be needing any of that, will you?
Get 10 Scorpid Worker Tails for Gornek in the Den.

$C{Priest}! I thought I would die out here with none to know of it. While I was hunting the scorpids of the Valley, I came across a particularly vicious-looking one. Hurling myself at it, I managed to inflict a massive blow to its claw before it closed around my leg.

I wasn't ready for its stinger though, and it sliced down and into my chest, cutting into my flesh and letting my blood. Please, you must kill the scorpid for me! My honor must be upheld! I fought it up on the plateau to the south.
Kill Sarkoth and bring his claw back to Hana'zua.

I trust the Valley of Trials will teach you much, young $c{priest}.

I was sent to the Valley to guide you, but I have discovered a growing taint here...

A group that calls itself the Burning Blade has a coven here in the Valley of Trials.  They are skulking in a cave to the northeast, and their Vile Familiars have spilled from its mouth to cause havoc.

As your first task against the Burning Blade, I bid you, defeat these familiars. Slay many and, if you survive, return to me.

Kill 12 Vile Familiars.

Return to Zureetha Fargaze outside the Den.
I am very interested in examining the hides from the deviate creatures who have infested these caves. Have you had any luck in collecting some, $c{shaman}?

Your efforts shall not go unnoticed in gathering these hides, $N.

Thank you for your dedication.

Ah, while you were gone a tablet came for you, $N.

Read it when you have time. If I'm not mistaken, it came from the $c{priest} trainer Ken'jai. He would have words with you when you're ready.
Read the Hallowed Tablet and speak to Ken'jai outside the Den in the Valley of Trials.

So ya made it... good good! Da spirits tol' me you be comin' to see Ken'jai soon enough. Let me be one o' da first to welcome ya to da Valley of Trials. Dis place not be your home fer long, but while it is, why dontcha make da best o' it.

As ya test yeself, ya'll find ya have better an' better control o'er da spirits--ya'll be callin' on dem fer greata an' greata tings...  dat's where ol' Ken'jai come in. You come talk to ole Ken'jai when ya feel yer ready. If da spirits agree, den we see 'bout teachin' ya more powerful abilities... but only if da spirits agree.

Go now, talk to da rest of da Valley's people. Speak to me again later.

While you were helping me out, this rune was given to me to pass on to you. Take some time to read it when you have a chance. I'm thinkin' it came from the $c{rogue} trainer Solm. Take a gander at it and go find him inside Anvilmar when you've a chance.
Read the Encrypted Rune and speak to Solm Hargrin in Coldridge Valley.

You made it! Great!

We've got an influx of activity lately, so I'm glad to count another of the Ironforge clan among our numbers. Nothin' like a cold blade in your hand and a shadow to keep you one step ahead, and if you're here, you know exactly what I mean!

Anyway, as you start peekin' around Coldridge you'll probably have need of training at some point. You just come back to me whenever you feel you need it and I'll teach you what I know--a trick here, a maneuver there. You know, the stuff that keeps you alive and makin' a little extra coin.

Keep an eye out on our gnomish friends too... they kinda got the short end of the stick what with Gnomeregan being... destroyed. They'll need our help to feel welcome.

It sure gets hot out here in the Valley of Trials.

<Galgar wipes his brow.>

If only I had some cactus apples, I could make my famous cactus apple surprise! Nothing cools you off faster than a piece of that delicious treat.

I'll tell you what, $N. If you bring me 10 cactus apples, I'll make you a few portions of cactus apple surprise to take with you on your adventures, and a free training manual, too. If you're interested, you can find cactus apples growing near the cactus plants around here.
Bring Galgar 10 Cactus Apples. You remember him saying that they could be found near cactuses.
Have you finished collecting cactus apples?
Wonderful, $N! As promised, here is your cactus apple surprise. Pick one of these training manuals, too. I've got plenty to go around.

Finally, you are of age, $N... of age to battle in the name of the Horde. To conquer for the glory of the Warchief.

Yes...

<Kaltunk looks you over.>

You will do nicely.

No doubt you wish to find a great dragon or demon and strangle it with your bare hands, but perhaps it would be wise to start on something less... dangerous.

<Kaltunk laughs.>

Report to Gornek, he should be able to assign a task better suited to a young $c{priest}. You will find Gornek in the Den, to the west.
Speak with Gornek. You recall Kaltunk marking your map with his location and mentioning that Gornek resided in the Den, a building to the west.

Another one of Kaltunk's recruits, hm?

A sorry state of affairs we find ourselves in if this is the best the Horde can produce. No matter. By the time we think you're ready to leave the Valley, you'll be a proud warrior of the Horde.

Cursed peons!  They work hard gathering lumber from the trees of the valley, but they're always taking naps!  I need someone to help keep the peons in line.

You look like the right $r{troll} for my task.  Here, you take this blackjack and use it on any lazy peons you find sleeping on the job.  A good smack will get them right back to work!  Return the blackjack when you're done.

Lousy slacking peons...
Use the Foreman's Blackjack on Lazy Peons when they're sleeping.  Wake up 5 peons, then return the Foreman's Blackjack to Foreman Thazz'ril in the Valley of Trials.
Another delivery! Fantastic. Set it over by the pile and we can discuss your compensation.

Thank you for your hard work, $N. There has been an uprising in bandits and thieves intercepting trade routes as of late. If you find other crates lying around, please bring them here and we'll handle the rest.

Here is your payment.

Thank you for your service to Zephras, young $c{rogue}.

The vuldren are typically quite docile, but the animals that call Zephras home can sense when the magic on the winds is out of balance, which can lead to dangerous and unpredictable behavior if left unchecked.
Excellent work, $N. You'd make a fine ranger if this whole "adventurer" thing doesn't work out for you.

The Al'Aketh cult is a blight upon this island. These cultists are surely the ones responsible for agitating the simple wind sprites that reside here and turning them violent.

Regrettably, we'll need to disperse these roiling winds here before they harm someone. We also need to send a clear message to the cult that they are not welcome in the grove.

Will you lend me your aid, $c{rogue}?
Slay 6 Roiling Winds and 7 Al'Aketh Converts in Thendal Grove.
It pains me to shed shen'dorei blood here in the grove, but we do what we must.

You've done enough here, $c{rogue}. I'll stay and clean up any stragglers down there.

Head back to the Village and tell Rorian about the cult's presence. He will not be pleased.
Bring word of the Al'Aketh to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove.

This is most troubling, but unfortunately unsurprising. We've been aware of the cult's movements for some time, but we've been content to watch from afar. Their agitation of the wind spirits near the standing stones is a clear escalation on their part.

You've performed a difficult but necessary service for Thendal Grove, $N. Thank you.

Rorian informed you that I've been watching you. I now offer you a test of resolve. However, be warned--it will send you into great danger.

Go to the caves to the west. Thin out the ursera's numbers there, and find their matriarch, one the rangers call "Urs'anah". Put her down and bring me proof of her demise. Once you have done that, you will have taken an important step on your path.
Slay 8 Ursera Scavengers and collect the head of the den mother, Urs'anah in Thendal Grove.
What I ask of you is not easy, but you must be prepared for much greater challenges if you are to survive long enough to be of service to Zephras Isle.
Very well done. You've felled beasts and laid low cultist interlopers. You have shown great promise but your path must soon take you beyond the relative safety of Thendal Village.

You may not realize this but everything you've done has been a trial of sorts. A test for what is to come for you. It's a big island out there, and Zephras needs spirited young adventurers such as yourself if we are to survive the trials our people face.

The one called Aetheen of the Gales is one of the leaders of our people here on Zephras Isle, and she has been watching you. She has a task that you must complete. Speak with her to learn more.
Speak with Aetheen of the Gales in Thendal Grove.

Rorian has told me much of you. I am likely unknown to you, but I am a member of the Council of Elders here on Zephras Isle. I've come to read the flow of the winds here in Thendal Grove. I'm also here to assess young shen'dorei such as yourself that are coming of age.

So tell me, are you ready to take your next step? Are you ready to serve Zephras Isle?

One of the most pervasive threats on Zephras Isle is the Al'Aketh Cult. They are religious zealots devoted to the worship of the supposed elemental ruler of Skywall, Al'Akir the Windlord. They are brutal, single-minded, and their power and ambitions are growing more deadly by the day.

Your path will soon take you to Shen'dar Village to the south. Present yourself to Constable Aonda when you arrive. The cult threatens Shen'dar and they are in need of aid. Tell Aonda that I sent you.
Report to Constable Aonda in Shen'dar Village.
Aetheen sent you, then? I'll confess, you don't look like much to me, but Shen'dar Village won't turn down willing aid, much less aid sent from Elder Aetheen herself.

The ursera den to the southwest is rapidly becoming a problem. Just last week the rangers had to kill an adolescent ursera who wandered too close to the village and attempted to attack a boy playing near the base of the elder tree in the center of the village.

We were fortunate that the boy escaped with his life. Hunger and desperation makes these beasts too dangerous to be left unchecked. Go south and put the scrawniest among the ursera down. Bring me their claws as proof when it is done.
Collect 6 Scrawny Ursera Claws from Scrawny Ursera in Thendal Grove.
The ursera have grown far more aggressive of late. I wonder what has changed to cause this shift in behavior?
Well done, $c{rogue}. The Rangers of the Grove are in your debt.

While you were away dealing with our vuldren problem, our resident $c{rogue} trainer--Akeri Duskblade--has requested to speak with you. He left this note, so read that first, then seek him out inside the watchtower, here in the village.

He's a shady fellow, but then again, so are you. I think you'll get along well.
Read the Simple Note then speak with Akeri Duskblade within the watchtower in Thendal Grove.

I almost did not hear you approach me, young $c{rogue}.

Almost.

Almost won't be good enough when you leave Thendal Grove. You must be a slender blade, silent and steady. Ever vigilant and ever mindful of your surroundings. You might have what it takes to survive the dangers of Zephras. You also might end up with your throat slit in a ditch. Ultimately that's entirely up to you.

Speak with me again if you wish to take your next steps.

You've got that "Windshaper" air about you. Something about how I can feel a tiny bit of static on my skin when near someone spirit-touched that gives it away. Before I properly put you to work around here, you should check in with our resident Windshaper elder, Illaya Amberwind. She's just outside, near the center of town.

Oh, and check in with Coriella Calmbreeze as well, she runs the local inn and can provide lodging and supplies, should you need them.
Speak with Illaya Amberwind and Coriella Calmbreeze in Shen'dar Village.

Checked in with Illaya then? Great. Lots of tension between the High Order and the Windshapers these days, but they keep things civil here in Shen'dar. Everyone here is well aware that we've got bigger problems than their quibbles.

Now that that's done, you look like someone who might be looking for something to do with their hands and I've got a bandit problem that I was hoping you could help me with.

As if bandits and mad cultists weren't enough, the hills are thick with prideclaws as well right now. They are starting to encroach on the village borders and growing bolder by the day. It's only a matter of time before someone's pet or child is taken. It would be a mercy for us to cull their numbers now rather than after some tragedy occurs.

Bring me a dozen or so of their pelts. I can turn them into all sorts of goods that will be of aid to the village.
Collect 10 Prideclaw Pelts from the Prideclaws in Shen'dar Highlands.
If you ask me, I think Prideclaws are actually kind of cute. From a safe distance... and while standing behind someone holding a sword, of course.
I didn't say it wouldn't be a dirty job, did I?

A flock of Hippogryph have recently established nesting grounds southeast of Shen'dar Village and they've been wreaking havoc on travelers on the road. I need someone to head down there and thin them out for us.
Slay 8 Hippogryph Youths, 6 Hippogryph Protectors and a Hippogryph Matriarch in the Shen'dar Highlands.
Well done, and quickly too. Not too bad at all.

There's a cave not far to the north, hidden behind a waterfall. It's well known to me that there's a group of bandits that are operating out of that cave. They were a problem for us before the cult arrived, but now they are a real terror. I can't spare the people to go and clear them out, unfortunately.

I need you to go there and take care of them for me. Kill as many as you can, and if possible, take out their leader, the one they call "Badwind" Bennic. That cave is dangerous, so be careful.
Kill 10 Highlands Bandits and their leader, "Badwind" Bennic in the Shen'dar Highlands.

With the bandits dispersed, that is one less problem for us to deal with. Though I confess that now I worry that any bandits who survived may turn next to the cult for protection, further bolstering their increasingly alarming numbers.

Still though, we'll take the victories where we can get them.

The faithful of Al'Akir grow ever stronger with each eager new recruit like yourself. As you can see, our strength gives form to the storm itself!

Normally I'd send you straight to Skypriest Aanders for assessment, but he is occupied at present receiving a guest at the inn on the north side of town. Please avoid that place for now. An unshaven recruit like yourself in the presence of such a guest would be inappropriate.

For now, just don't get in anyone's way.
Look around Falaath Village to learn about the cult's intentions in the Shen'dar Highlands.

Lorthuna herself was there? She's the leader of the whole damned cult!

If they are making a move on Shen'dar Village and the western watchtower, we've got to be ready. What is strange is... why the watchtower?

The Village I can understand, but the tower? It doesn't have much strategic significance, other than as a minor lookout post.

Regardless, we will be prepared for them. They'll find that highlanders aren't as easy to catch flat footed as they might think.

It gladdens my heart that you wish to serve Al'Akir. Our current trials as a people stem from our own complacency. We grew prideful and took the bounty of the winds for granted. The stagnation that followed is the reason the spirits of the wind abandoned us.

Only through acts of contrition may we feel the wind's caress once more. If you seek the fellowship of like-minded shen'dorei, go to Falaath Village and find Missionary Jasaan there. I will mark you so that the faithful will know you as a recruit.

Report to Missionary Jasaan near the entrance to Falaath Village.

If you lose your Mark of Akir, speak with Sania Silverstream in Shen'dar Village to regain the effect.

What is this? A new acolyte seeking to serve the windlord sent by sister Sania? Truly we are blessed by the touch of the four winds this day!

We welcome all who seek to bask in the blessings of Al'Akir.

A band of Al'Aketh cult ruffians have taken up residence near the temple ruins just southwest of here, led by a real monster called Malduko Cloudcrush. This rabble has no doubt been dispatched here by High Priestess Lorthuna at the Shrine of Akir to attack travelers and coerce our people into joining the cult.

I need to stay here at my post to alert travelers leaving the grove of the danger, but I would be grateful if you could do something about those cultists and their leader for me.
Slay 6 Al'Aketh Brutes, 4 Al'Aketh Neophytes, and Malduko Cloudcrush in Thendal Grove.

It was all I could do to stop myself from going over and joining you from my position here. I can only hope that these louts got the message and clear out of here soon. 

Thank you, $c{rogue}. You have the gratitude of the Rangers of Thendal Grove.

Our best defense here might just be a strong offense. The advantage we now have is that we expect an attack is coming. What they won't expect is for us to hit them first.

I've already asked a lot of you, but please head back over to Falaath Village. Kill as many cultists as you can and if you can get close enough, kill the commander and bring me his head. I'll stay here and organize the citizens and our few peacekeepers to prepare a defense... just in case you don't return.
Travel to the ruins of Falaath Village and slay 6 Al'Aketh Stormcallers, 4 Living Lightning and take the head of Commander Cyclas.
It feels good to turn the tables on these zealots.

Thank the winds you've returned!

Sania Silverstream snuck out of town just before you returned, no doubt fleeing at the sight of our people arming themselves.

You've done an incredible thing for the people of Shen'dar Village and we owe you a debt of gratitude. If the cult returns to the highlands, they will find that Shen'dar is not such an easy target.

Winds guide you, $N.

I overheard you might be going to Falaath Village? While you are there, please keep an eye out for our stolen supply caches.

The Al'Aketh have been raiding our supply caravans carrying various goods such as food and windstones to and from the lowlands for months. They've been blaming the bandits, of course, but we all know that it all ends up in the same place. If there's any of that stuff left in Falaath, it would be a huge help if you could recover it.
Collect 10 packs of Stolen Shen'dar Supplies from Falaath Village in the Shen'dar Highlands.
There's a lot of hungry and desperate skyborne here who need these supplies.

This is great! We've been barely squeaking by without our regular supply deliveries. I'll work with the constable to ensure that these supplies get redistributed to the townsfolk who are in most dire need.

Up for a bit of work? I could use a bit of muscle from a strong adventuring-type such as yourself. With how dangerous things are getting around here, no one's had much time to hunt or forage of late, and I need someone to get out there and source me fresh eggs and strider meat to keep this village fed.

I'd be happy to teach you one of my famous recipes if you can bring me what I need. What do you say?
Collect 3 Small Eggs and 8 Strider Meat from creatures found throughout the Shen'dar Highlands.
No matter how much things change here on Zephras and how uncertain things get, I always say that a pipe full of dried peacebloom and nice full belly is a comfort that can't be beat!

These eggs aren't easy to get but wind save me, they are DELICIOUS fried up in a bit of ursera tallow.

If you've got a bit of time to spare and you enjoy cooking, I can teach you a few tips and tricks I've picked up. Say the word and I'd be happy to train you.

For now it seems the pylon and the village are safe, so I'd like you to deliver this report to Valennia Stormfist in Valanaar, at the southeastern edge of the island. Valennia is the leader of the peacekeepers on the island and she needs to know what happened here.

The cult is expanding rapidly and the peacekeepers have avoided direct conflict until now, but those days are over. Valanaar will need to be ready for a fight.

At any rate, thank you. You'll always have friends in Shen'dar, $N.
Deliver Aonda's Written Report to Valennia Stormfist in Valanaar.
A letter from Aonda. What's that crafty highlander been up to?

<Valennia's expression darkens as she reads the letter.>

Aonda trusted you to deliver this and she speaks highly enough of you in this letter, so I'll try to trust you too. Before we speak further, I need to consult with the few peacekeepers we have left here and formulate a plan in case the cult strikes here next. Enjoy your stay in Valanaar for now.

If you are looking to keep yourself busy, there are plenty of townsfolk that can likely use the help of a strong young adventurer like yourself.

<Illaya smiles warmly at you.>

I am glad you returned to speak with me, child of the winds. I knew it the first moment you walked into my presence, that you were strong in the skysight. Do you find this surprising? Even those who have not trained as a Shaman may possess the gift. 

Come, let us speak about the mandate of the Windshapers, the nature of our struggles on Zephras, and the plight of our people.
Listen to what Illaya Amberwind has to say.

I think you now understand how important the mission of the Windshapers is. Every soul who commands the skysight is of vital importance if we hope to establish dialogue with the spirits of the winds once again.

Between threats from within such as the Al'Aketh, and the uncertainty of our safety here in Skywall, it is our responsibility as Windshapers to use our gifts to save our home and ensure that the Shen'dorei can survive these trying times.

As a Windshaper, you have the ability to use the sacred skysight gifted to us by the elemental spirits. Travel to the standing stones to the northeast of the village. Find the elemental convergence there and use your gift.

You'll find that you may draw upon the skysight anywhere, but its boon is much more powerful if you do so in the presence of an elemental convergence. You may at times receive other bits of wisdom from the spirits that are drawn to such places of power, as well.
Use your Skysight racial ability at the Elemental Convergence in Thendal Grove.

Like a muscle, your skysight must be exercised if you hope to grow stronger in the gift. Leveraging your skysight to bridge the distance between the mortal and the spiritual may prove invaluable to you in your adventures.

You'd do well to remember what you've learned here today. Our ability to use our gifts to hear what the elements tell us could be the key to our survival.

H--Hello, stranger. You have the look of a capable adventurer about you. I...

<The Skyborne man winces, clearly suffering terrible pain>

...I was wondering if you were seeking employment? I came here to Valanaar to recruit fighters to help save my farm. If you are interested, please go find my wife Aamelia Windfield at our orchard to the west of Valanaar, in the lowlands.
Listen to what Alvarion Windfield has to say and find Aamelia Windfield at the Windfield Orchard.

<Aamelia listens while you explain what became of Alvarion.>

At least I know he's going to be safe in Valanaar.

Stranger, I hate to tell you this but I think my idiot husband likely just sent you here to die for nothing. If you have any sense at all, you should leave now. This isn't your fight.

Oh, so you've got more courage than sense, then? Fine, I won't argue.

Ferauu and his goons aren't due to pick up their take of the harvest just yet, so I'm going to put you to work for your meals until they arrive.

Head outside and gather today's batch of stormapples for me. Oh, and the bandits lurking around the stormapple trees... They think they are sneaky. They aren't. Kill them for me. 

Let's see what you've got in a fight.
Gather 10 Ripe Stormapples and slay 5 Hungry Bandits at the Windfield Orchard.

These bandits are more likely to double cross and steal from each other than they are to steal from normal folks. I bet if Ferauu knew some of his people went $c{rogue} and came here early to tamper with the harvest, he'd kill them himself.
I watched you take down those bandits from the window. Not bad.

I'm sure you've noticed the giant flutterflies out in the outer fields near the orchard? They are pleasant to look at, but they also have other benefits; namely their wing dust. It can be a mess, but if you can gather it up in large amounts, it has useful household applications.

Take this Flutterfly Swatter and give the big bugs a good swat for me. They'll usually just get scared and flee, but sometimes they'll take some offense. Either way, they'll give their rumps a shake and drop a pile of dust.
Gather 5 Flutterfly Dust from the Flutterflies around the Gustberry Lowlands.
Flutterflies are normally docile and calm, but rub them the wrong way and sometimes they'll surprise you.

This stuff can be a bit messy and it tends to get everywhere. You'll probably be shaking this out of your trousers for weeks, unfortunately. I do appreciate it, though. I've had this on my to-do list for weeks, but getting too far from the house when it's just me on my own with bandits lurking everywhere is a big risk.

Don't bother asking me what I use this stuff for. Things. Stuff and things. Don't worry about it.

As if the harvest wasn't light enough this year already, the galestriders in the area have been getting into the orchard and stealing my stormapples. Think you can head out to the fields and cull them for me?

Take care though stranger, these lowlands galestriders are bigger and angrier than the highlands variety. Watch yourself. A well-timed kick is all it takes to put you down for good if you aren't paying attention.

Bring me some of their meat and I can make us a hot meal with it as well.
Gather 7 Lowlands Galestrider Tenderloins from the Ornery Galestriders found throughout the Gustberry Lowlands.
I don't think I've had real meat for dinner in... well, too long.
These are big tenderloins! You must have taken down some real monsters out there.

The bandits have camps all over and there's a small one in the hills just north of here. Head up there and start cracking skulls. If we can catch them off guard and take them out before they come for us, we might just even the odds enough to stand a chance.

Bring me their masks. The bloodier the better.
Loot 7 Blood-Stained Bandit Masks from Highwayman Bandits in the Gustberry Lowlands.

If you manage to bring me enough bandit masks, maybe I'll stitch a blanket out of them and give it to Ferauu.

<Aamelia laughs loudly.>

When I said the bloodier the better, you really listened. Good. It lets me know you made it hurt.

On a serious note, thank you for what you've done so far. I've been floating aimlessly around this farm for weeks as if I was just waiting for the end to come. I think I'm starting to have hope again.

Ferauu and his thugs are due any time now. All that's left is to go out and face them. What do you say, will you see this through to the end with me?

You've done a lot to give us a fighting chance. Even if we die today, we'll at least know we gave it our best shot.

This is your last chance, stranger. If you want to head back to Valanaar and live another day, I wouldn't blame you.

On the other hand, if you really have a thing for lost causes just let me know when you are ready to go. We'll walk out there with our heads held high and whatever happens, happens.
Speak with Aamelia Windfield when you are ready to confront the bandit leader.
I... can't believe it's over. I need to stop and calm myself before my heart leaps right out of my chest.

<You lean in close to try and hear the words coming from beneath the giant construct's armor plates.>

...Function error...

...Question...

...What is....

...Function...

<These fragmented words and phrases seem to just repeat. Maybe someone nearby knows more about this construct?>
Speak with Aamelia Windfield about the Malfunctioning Cyclone Construct.

The construct? It's been wandering around the fields for decades. Since the wind elementals left us, I think. Alvarion suspected that it used to haul harvests to market, or maybe tend to livestock back before this was an orchard. That could have been a thousand years ago though.

In the old days, the Windshapers used to maintain these constructs. We've talked about petitioning them to come and take a look at it, but it's never been a pressing concern to us. Mostly we just ignore it these days.

Now that you've arrived in Valanaar, you'll likely want to check in with the other members of the Windshapers here. The current Grand Skyseer and her people operate out of the lodge near the center of Valanaar.

You should also be aware, the Windshapers and High Order don't get along very well in these parts. Be careful and give the High Order a good, wide berth. We've got enough to worry about with the cult, I won't tolerate faction violence in the streets of Valanaar.

Elder Amberwind sent me a message about you and your exploits in Shen'dar Village. You are most welcome here, friend.

You have a strong aura, and you clearly have a resonance with the spirits. Fewer and fewer of us have the skysight of late, and Zephras needs those with the gift if we are to survive these trying times. I am glad you have found your way to me.

I look forward to further making your acquaintance.

I guess it doesn't feel quite right to keep calling you stranger after all of this so... thank you, $N. 

If you wouldn't mind and are back out that way, please let Alvarion know what happened here. Also, tell him that once he's up on his feet he needs to bring a windshaper back here to look at that construct for us to make sure it's safe to have around our... our family.

<Aamelia touches her belly gently.>

He doesn't know about this part. Let's just keep that bit between us for now.
Speak with Alvarion Windfield in Valanaar.

<Alvarion's eyes tear up as you finish retelling the story of what happened at the orchard.>

I don't know how to thank you, friend. I came to Valanaar looking for hope. A vain hope, I was almost certain. But instead I found a hero. A real hero, like the stories from before we came to Skywall. 

I'll never forget what you did for us, $N. You'll always be welcome at the Windfield home.

The Windshapers have been hard at work trying to respond to the current crisis on Zephras Isle. We have made several surprising discoveries in our search for the missing wind spirits, and we are developing a plan of action that could help us gain the means to save the island.

We'll need strong young adventurers like yourself for this to work however. Please, if you have a moment, let us speak on this further.
Listen to what Ayessa Dawnsinger has to say.

So now you see? There is a world of knowledge and untapped potential outside of Skywall. This will never stop being our home, but I've come to believe that the path to our salvation lies below. We must travel to Azeroth and gain the power and means to save Zephras Isle. This is the way.

Will you have the courage to join us when the time comes?

You may or may not be aware of this, but Sania Silverstream over there is a "missionary" for the Al'Aketh. They like to play at being a normal religious order and send non-threatening emissaries around to recruit. We've tolerated Sania so far to avoid direct conflict with the cult, but it's obvious the illusion of peace won't last much longer.

You are new here and unknown to most, so I'd like to see if you can use Sania to get close to the cult and find out what their plans are for the village.
Speak with Sania Silverstream in Shen'dar Village.

Greetings child, my name is Sania Silverstream and I am a junior priestess in the Order of the Al'Aketh. Do you wish to learn more of our sovereign, the Windlord Al'Akir?

There is always room at the Windlord's table for the righteous and the repentant.

Are you familiar with Windsong Crawlers? You see, these crabs are native only to Windsong Lake here on Zephras, and they are only able to be harvested a few weeks of the year.

With all of the cult activity of late, I've not been able to get out to the lake to harvest them, and our window is rapidly closing. I'd be appreciative if you could go and gather some for me. They can generally be found along the shorelines around the lake and in rivers.

Do be careful though, they are meaner than they look!
Collect 6 pieces of Windsong Crawler Meat.

Windsong Crawler meat is common enough here but it was something of a delicacy on the islands of Anvilas and Siroccas. Was a time, back when the skystreams were open that the locals would mob me for the stuff when I'd make the trip to Shen'dramar or New Eldre'naar.

Not been able to visit those places in... well... a long time.

Winds bless me, this meat looks fantastic! 

Thank you so much, $c{rogue}.

By order of Constable Aonda of the Peacekeepers, a bounty is hereby placed upon the scourge of the highlands, Vulgara the Insatiable. Last spotted on a hilltop rise just southwest of Shen'dar Village, the winged vuldren terror is highly dangerous and should be approached with caution.

Deliver the beast's head to Danarii Bellowveil to receive your reward.
Kill Vulgara the Insatiable in the Shen'dar Highlands and bring her head to Danarii Bellowveil.
I'll need the creature's head as proof of the deed.

If we didn't have enough on our plates between the cult and the highlands bandits, we don't need a giant vuldren terrorizing our citizens as well. You've done a great thing here today. As promised, here is your reward.

We are relying on windstones more and more for day-to-day living here on Zephras so we try and maintain a cache of them in reserve for emergencies. Lately I've noticed some go missing from our stores.

We've found windstones on bandits we've captured recently, and I suspect they are behind our shortages.

If you find yourself near the bandit cave to the north, mind knocking a few heads together and reclaiming some of our pilfered windstones for me?
Collect 10 Pilfered Windstones from the Highlands Bandits in the Shen'dar Highlands.

These sneakthieves have likely been breaking into our supplies for months. I tried to convince Aonda to put a raid together to clear out that bandit cave for good, but she didn't want to pull the few peacekeepers we have away from the village. 

With the cultists at Falaath Village to the south growing in numbers, I suppose I can't fault her for that.
Thanks $c{rogue}. This should help us get by for now. If we can't get the supply routes squared away soon though, a few stolen windstones will be the least of our worries.

Thank you very much for these. As elves we all have a deep connection to magic and these windstones are becoming more and more precious as the magic imbued into this island by the great anchor pylons continues to fade. 

Windstones aren't the only beneficial thing you can harvest from the land. Please, take one of these manuals.

Historically, the Windshapers have seen to the tending of the magical instruments and devices that were gifted to us by the spirits of the wind. This includes the myriad of magical constructs around the island. Since the spirits left us, only a scant few of these are still functional.

One of the few remaining working constructs in Valanaar has become damaged. One of our artisans was dispatched to help, but he may be in need of aid. Travel to the west end of the city and offer any assistance you can.
Find Riaani Nightwind on the west side of Valanaar.

<Riaani's face is buried under the heaving armor plates of the construct, attempting to work on the mechanisms underneath. He does not notice your presence at all.>

Storms curse--where is the core?! Who thought it would be a good idea to remove the Gyrozephyr as well? It's a miracle this construct's winds haven't dissipated entirely by now!

The paramount concern of the Windshapers is to better understand why the spirits left us, and what we may be able to do to bring them back. One curious fixture of Shadowgale Forest to the north is the presence of a curious form of wind sprite that some call "hollows". We know little of them and why they are there, but we do know that they first started to appear after the spirits of the wind left us.

I need you to go there and disperse them. Gather the remains and bring them back here.
Gather 10 Wind Hollow Essences from Wind Hollows in the Shadowgale Forest.

Oh, hello. Ayessa sent you to assist me? Very well then. 

Not sure what an obvious novice like yourself can do, but if you give me a moment to pull my head out of this construct's innards I might have a few ideas of things you can do to help.
Speak with Riaani Nightwind and listen to what he has to say.

Whatever reason the cult has for attacking the tower, it's not worth losing our people over.

I'd like for you to head to the southwest and check in on that watchtower for us. Find the peacekeepers there and tell them to head back to the village. Holding that tower is not worth the lives it would cost and I'd rather concentrate the defenders we do have here to protect our citizens.

Peacekeeper Vaaniel is in charge; let him know to head back here as quickly as possible. Hurry!
Find Peacekeeper Vaaniel at the western watchtower.

<The body here is somewhat fresh, clearly only recently having been killed. Judging by the burns and scorch marks on this peacekeeper's skin, it's clear that they were killed by the cult's storm-wielding spellcasters.>
<As you inspect the body of the dead peacekeeper, a bloody note falls free of his hands. Picking it up and reading it may give you a clue as to how to proceed from here.>
Collect the note you found near the dead peacekeeper and read it to determine your next steps.
What news from the western watch?

So they are all dead, then. Storms curse these cult bastards!

While you managed to take out the priest and stop the cultists at the tower, I confess that I'm now doubly concerned about whatever it was you said that they were doing to the pylon. The fact that there was such a massive cache of windstones there with them tells me that they needed enormous energy for it.

I have to wonder, what's the end goal here? Violating the pylon, attacking the village? To what end?

Since you are going to Valanaar anyway, please deliver the signet ring you recovered from the tower to Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. 

He will want this back, and more importantly, he will want to learn the fate of his nephew. Talaanis is the High Elder of Zephras Isle and more importantly, he is a good man who is well loved by the people, despite our current hardships. It pains me to think of how he will react to this news. Please express my condolences for his loss.
Deliver the Shadowsong Family Signet to Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.
What is that you have for me? Oh... oh no.

I... am very sorry to hear that my nephew is dead. I thank you kindly for recovering this, and bringing it to me.

It's not common that such capable young shen'dorei come down from the highlands. If you need work, please speak with Valennia Stormfist, the captain of the peacekeepers here in Valanaar. These days we need all the help we can get.

We've been bugged.

It's skyhopper season in the lowlands, which means the pests are everywhere. One of the High Order mages reported that one of the insects that they killed had an enchantment of some kind placed upon it. When we inspected it closely it seems to be some sort of listening spell.

We suspect that the cult is using these enchanted insects as spies. Go and exterminate them for us. You won't be able to tell which are enchanted by looking at them, so you'll just have to kill them all.
Kill Skyhoppers in Valanaar until you've eliminated 8 Enchanted Skyhoppers.
I'm sure there are more of these critters around Valanaar, but every enchanted skyhopper we stomp out makes the city just a tiny bit safer.

The hippogryphs that have taken up residence southwest of the village can be a nuisance, but they also present a rather unique opportunity to obtain their feathers. Many skyborne love to adorn their hair with vibrant plumes and the down feathers of a hippogryph are exceptionally vibrant and, more importantly, silky soft.

If you are heading that way, try and gather as many of the fallen feathers as you can from around their nesting grounds. Do be careful, as wild hippogryph are not tolerant of guests.
Collect 8 Hippogryph Down feathers in the Shen'dar Highlands.
What beautiful things did you bring me?

It might seem a bit of a vain triviality, gathering feathers for our hair. However, even in times like these, one needs to embrace the small joys as much as possible. 

If one thing I create brings someone joy, then I will consider that to be a good day. Thank you for bringing me these and helping me bring some joy to Zephras.

Be warned, members of the High Order have been seen in the vicinity of the standing stones north of the village. We have warned them time and again to not meddle at our sacred sites, but they are growing more bold in pushing us. Prove your resolve to us by going to the standing stones and dispersing them.

I am loathe to condone outright bloodshed, but do what you must to drive them off. Return to me when it's done.
Slay 6 High Order Apprentices in Shen'dar Highlands.

Direct conflict with our shen'dorei brothers and sisters only weakens us as a people, but decisive action must at times be taken to prevent greater tragedy.

The mages of the High Order have zero regard for the consequences of their magical meddling. The forces that bind our island are fragile and vulnerable and all it could take is one thoughtless action to destroy our home.

A moment if you will, $N. Are you headed towards Shadowgale Forest? There is a druid conclave there in a cave to the northeast. I have been waiting on word from them but their correspondence is long overdue.

With Ban'aethall in ruins and all the unrest lately I worry something dire may have happened. Please, if you are able, go seek out Elegael Thornpaw and put my mind at ease.
Find and speak with Elegael Thornpaw in the northeastern part of Shadowgale Forest.

You look like a capable adventurer. Do you happen to be headed towards Shadowgale Forest? Ban'aethal lies deep in the forest; that's where we're all from.

<Ealaane gestures to the other refugees.>

We've recently had to evacuate Ban'aethal, as it began to fall into the sky. It was sudden and in the middle of the night. If you are headed that way, would you please look for any belongings left behind? The forest and village are far too dangerous for us to return to now.
Collect 8 Abandoned Belongings from the ruins of Ban'aethal.

If you are traveling to Ban'aethal, I have a selfish request. My love, Resaan... I believe is no longer a part of this world. He had tried to go back to get supplies even though I begged him to stay. It has been over a week already and I fear the worst.

Please, if you find him, bring him home. If he has perished then I beg you to please bring me his heirloom.
Find Resaan in the Ruins of Ban'aethal.
The Fate of a Loved One

Greetings, $c{rogue}. I can see you've got the look of an adventurer about you. This is good. The world needs more of us restless souls, seeking fortune and glory.

You'll need to learn to thrive in the wilds to be successful in this line of work. Not sure how your outdoor skills are but I can probably teach you a thing or two, if you'd be apt to learn.

Have a seat near the fire and get comfortable. I'll walk you through it.
Sit near Raan's Basic Campfire and wait until you receive the Boosted Rest buff.

So now that we've learned the basics, why don't you go and learn a tradeskill from the trainers in the village nearby. They will also teach you how to create a camp fixture suitable to your new profession.

So you want to learn more about camping, huh? Good for you, $c{rogue}. The first step any adventurer needs to take is to become a cook and learn how to make a campfire.

Cooking's not just about making tasty foods. It's also the foundation for your camp.
Speak with Zerril Softbreeze in Shen'dar Village to learn to become a cook.

With this, you'll be able to set up a camp anywhere out in the wilderness. What you've learned is just the basics, so you won't be able to place too many furnishings around it.

Raise your cooking skill and you might just be able to learn to make even bigger fires.

You can also learn the basics of furnishing your campsites from other tradeskill trainers if you're savvy in their skills.

With an influx of new recruits like yourself, it's been hard to keep our weapons supplied. Our weaponsmith, Kzan, is running low on training weapons and I'd like to see what kinds of skills you possess to get an idea of what I have to work with. Luckily for you, I have a solution to both.

While you're out there cutting your teeth on boars, salvage six abandoned training weapons. Our failed recruits left them laying on the ground. Once you do, return them to our weaponsmith Kzan behind me in the Den.
Collect 6 Abandoned Training Weapons, then return to Kzan Thornslash in the Den.

Throm'ka, $c{priest}. Gorak told me I should be expecting you. It is good to see you in one piece!

Were you able to collect the training weapons I requested?
Thank you for returning these weapons, $N. I will get to work repairing them for the next wave of recruits.

So, you've become a Blacksmith. That's a great choice if you want to make sure your blades never dull.

I reckon I know someone that can help with that by teaching you how to craft a Sharpening Wheel. Bring one of these out at your camp and all the warriors and rogues in the area will be lining up to hone their weapons.
Speak with Aedi Thriceforged in Shen'dar Village to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

There you have it, you can now craft your very own Sharpening Wheel. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.

So you've taken up First Aid? That's an honorable... and pragmatic pursuit as a $c{rogue}.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a First Aid Kit for your camp. Injuries are a reality in the world of adventuring and offering some much-needed healing at your camp could even save lives.
Speak with Naleeia Tattermend in Shen'dar Village to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

There you have it, you can now craft your very own First Aid Kit. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.

You might not think so, but your skill as a fisherman can actually come in handy at camp.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Fish Bowl for your camp. You can use this fixture to help provide a bit of joy to yourself and your fellow adventurers. A happy adventurer is a strong adventurer and I'm sure your combat capabilities will reflect that.
Speak with Fenn Fairweather in Shen'dar Village to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

There you have it, you can now craft your very own Fish Bowl. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.

Mining isn't the most glamorous, but it's good honest work and a fine profession for you to explore.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Lodestone for your camp. Build one of these and everyone who wants to swing a sword will be eager to gather round your fire and soak up the extra "oomph" it can provide to increase their combat prowess.
Speak with Messana Crestwind in Shen'dar Village to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

There you have it, you can now craft your very own Lodestone. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.

<A torn shipping label can be found on the side of the now fully stocked crate. Though the intended recipient is torn off, details of its origin still remain.

"Return damaged shipments or empty crates to the Durotar Supply and Logistics trade outpost, now conveniently located due west of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Your time is valuable and we will compensate you for your efforts!"

Beside the text is a crudely drawn map of the area near the aforementioned destination.>
Deliver the Shipping Label to someone at the Durotar Supply and Logistics trade hub near the Crossroads in the Barrens.

You there, stranger. Get low and keep quiet. We are not alone here.

I was on patrol near the border and noticed that there are a number of Al'Aketh skulking around the house just up the hill there to the north. I don't know what they are doing here, but it can't be good.

If you want to make yourself useful, get in there and take them out. I'll wait here and watch your back.
Kill 10 Al'Aketh Assassins in the Shen'dar Highlands.

I'm glad you made it back. That group of Al'Aketh looked like stone cold killers. 

Thank you for your aid, I'll include your assistance in my report when I return to Valanaar.
